objective: Let an administrator see, on the health surface they already have, whether this Brain is keeping up with reading what it holds and which effect classes it can perform — two readings Brain already computes and nothing reports. §9 makes an unread document something the auditor does not have and blocks its layer, yet nothing Brain-wide says how many documents are waiting to be read, stuck mid-read or unreadable: server/services/documents/queue.ts `extractionQueueDepth` (~94; `pending.length + inFlight.size`) has no caller anywhere, and `documents.extraction_status` (EXTRACTION_STATUSES in server/domain/types.ts ~517) is only read per document. Likewise server/services/effects/adapter.ts `listAdapters` (~183) has no caller, so which effect adapters are registered — and therefore which of §20's per-class guarantees this process can actually keep — is not answerable. GET /api/health (server/routes/health.ts ~23) already has an administrator-only branch carrying operator facts (revision, persistence, migrations, OCR, storage), which is exactly where these belong; the non-administrator branch must stay as it is.
expectedOutcome: A new server/services/documents/backlog.ts exports `readingBacklog()` returning `{ inProcess: number, byStatus: Record<ExtractionStatus, number>, missingFiles: number }`, where `inProcess` is `extractionQueueDepth()` (explicitly labelled as this process's in-memory queue, not the Brain's), `byStatus` counts registered documents by extraction_status over every value in EXTRACTION_STATUSES (zero where there are none, never omitted), and `missingFiles` counts rows with file_missing = 1 — one grouped query plus one count, in SQL sayable in both dialects. The administrator branch of GET /api/health gains `reading: await readingBacklog()` and `effects: listAdapters().map(({ name, effectClass, namespace }) => ({ name, effectClass, namespace }))` (names and classes only; no adapter function or configuration crosses). The non-administrator response is byte-for-byte the set of keys it is today.
nonGoals: Any threshold, alert or refusal driven by the backlog: §25's rule that storage and health are reported and stop no work applies.
Enqueueing, retrying or reprocessing anything from the health route; it performs no write.
Exposing document ids, filenames, paths or project names in the reading.
Changing the extraction queue, the effects engine or adapter registration.
Anything under server/services/identity/**, any policy entry, migration or schema change.

acceptanceConditions.statement: readingBacklog() over a database with documents in QUEUED, READY, BLOCKED and FAILED states returns those counts, returns 0 for every other value of EXTRACTION_STATUSES (every key present), counts file_missing rows in missingFiles, and passes on both backends.
As a Brain administrator GET /api/health includes `reading` and `effects`; each effects entry has exactly the keys name, effectClass and namespace.
As an ordinary project member GET /api/health returns exactly the keys it returns today (ok, schemaVersion, providers, ocr) and no `reading` or `effects`.
Two consecutive administrator reads of GET /api/health change no row count in documents, extraction_runs or work_items and enqueue no extraction (extractionQueueDepth unchanged).
The existing health and API suites (tests/api.test.ts, tests/access.test.ts) still pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Discard the branch. One new read-only module and two additive keys on the administrator branch of an existing read route; no schema, policy or write-path change.
